title: DET Speaking: Read Aloud, Speak About the Photo & the Interview
summary: Every DET speaking task — from reading a sentence aloud to the recorded interview universities watch — and how to sound clear and fluent.

nodes.label: Read / Listen, Then Speak
nodes.note: Respond to a written or spoken prompt

chunks.heading: Read Aloud & Speak About the Photo
chunks.body: **Read Aloud**: record yourself reading a sentence on screen — it scores **pronunciation and fluency**, so read at a steady, natural pace. **Speak About the Photo**: describe an image aloud for up to about **90 seconds** — keep talking, naming what you see and adding detail.
chunks.realExample: For Speak About the Photo, don't stop after 'It's a kitchen.' Add: who's there, what they're doing, colours, and a guess about the situation — filling the time fluently is what scores.
chunks.memoryHook: Read Aloud = steady & clear. Speak About the Photo = keep describing; never go silent.

chunks.heading: Read, Then Speak & Listen, Then Speak
chunks.body: You get a prompt — either **written (Read, Then Speak)** or **spoken (Listen, Then Speak)** — and then **speak your answer for up to ~90 seconds**. A quick mental plan (point → reason → example) keeps you fluent for the full time.
chunks.realExample: Prompt: 'Describe a place you'd like to visit and why.' Structure: name the place, one reason, one specific detail, a closing line — enough to fill 90 seconds without drying up.
chunks.memoryHook: Point → reason → example → close. A tiny plan fills the whole 90 seconds.

chunks.heading: The Speaking Sample — the one universities watch
chunks.body: Near the end you record a **longer Speaking Sample (a video interview)**: you pick a prompt and speak at length. This is **sent to the institutions** you apply to, so they hear your real fluency — treat it as the moment that matters most.
chunks.realExample: Choose the prompt you have the most to say about, take the short prep, and speak in clear, complete sentences — an admissions officer is literally watching this clip.
chunks.memoryHook: The Speaking Sample is your on-camera moment. Pick the prompt you can talk about most.

chunks.heading: Fluency and clarity beat a 'perfect' accent
chunks.body: The DET rewards **clear, intelligible, steady speech** — not a particular accent. Speak at a natural pace, finish your sentences, and avoid long pauses. A calm, clear answer scores better than a fast, tangled one.
chunks.realExample: If you lose your thread, pause briefly and rephrase rather than trailing into silence — recovering smoothly protects your fluency score.
chunks.memoryHook: Clear and steady wins. Your accent is fine; silence and stumbles are what cost marks.

recall.q: What does the 'Read Aloud' task score?
recall.a: Pronunciation and fluency — so you read the on-screen sentence at a steady, natural pace.

recall.q: How should you approach 'Speak About the Photo'?
recall.a: Describe the image aloud for up to about 90 seconds — keep talking, naming what you see and adding detail so you don't go silent.

recall.q: What's a reliable structure for the 'Then Speak' tasks?
recall.a: Point → reason → example → closing line, planned quickly, to stay fluent for the full ~90 seconds.

recall.q: Why does the Speaking Sample matter so much?
recall.a: It's a longer recorded video interview shared with the institutions you apply to, so they hear your real fluency.

recall.q: What does DET speaking reward more than a particular accent?
recall.a: Clear, intelligible, steady speech at a natural pace — accent isn't penalised, but pauses and stumbles cost marks.
